gaps.sentence: I ___ to contact him all week, but his phone is always engaged.
gaps.hint: all week repeated attempts until now
gaps.explanation: Repeated attempts continuing up to now take the present perfect continuous: have been trying.

gaps.sentence: Our team ___ the championship twice in the last five years.
gaps.hint: in the last five years up to now
gaps.explanation: 'In the last five years' is a period up to the present, so the present perfect fits: has won.

gaps.sentence: I ___ you were coming today — nobody told me!
gaps.hint: state verb forbids the past continuous
gaps.explanation: 'Know' is a state verb, so its past form is the past simple: didn't know.

gaps.sentence: When I got home, I realised I ___ my keys at the office.
gaps.explanation: 'Had left' — the leaving happened before the realising.

gaps.sentence: The wedding guests ___ when the string quartet began to play.
gaps.hint: in progress when the music began
gaps.explanation: An action in progress when a past event occurred takes the past continuous: were still arriving.

gaps.sentence: He ___ in the garden when the storm broke.
gaps.explanation: An action in progress interrupted by a short event — past continuous.

gaps.sentence: The train ___ faster than the bus, so we always take the train.
gaps.explanation: Timeless comparisons take the present simple: goes.

gaps.sentence: Every time I visit, she ___ something delicious from the garden.
gaps.hint: every time marks a repeated habit
gaps.explanation: 'Every time' marks a repeated action, which takes the present simple: brings.
